blocks.text: ORI:200–222 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

This final atomic block was reconsidered from first principles under delegated approval authority. The review compared five genuinely different candidate directions per root (45 candidates total), recorded 360 criterion scores, routed 115 English concepts and boundary cases, passed 18 canonical packet checks, passed 22 full Origin-family soundness checks, and preserved every deterministic generated form.

Approved architecture: ORI:2xx is the Origin relation layer for substrate-neutral ontological relations and capacities. The inward triplet owns source-grounding capacity; the outward triplet owns target-ground dependence; the systemic triplet owns shared-world constraint. Their third-trit contrast is persistent, operative, and latent.
ORI:200 — persistent source-grounding capacity — A persistent ontological capacity of one source to ground a specified state of affairs, independently of whether that capacity is presently operative.
ORI:201 — operative source-grounding capacity — An ontological capacity of one source that is presently operative in grounding a specified state of affairs.
ORI:202 — latent source-grounding capacity — An ontological capacity of one source to ground a specified state of affairs that belongs to it without being presently operative.

ORI:210 — persistent target-ground dependence — A persistent ontological relation under which one target's obtaining is conditional on a specified ground, independently of whether that dependence is presently operative.
ORI:211 — operative target-ground dependence — An ontological relation that is presently conditioning one target's obtaining on a specified ground.
ORI:212 — latent target-ground dependence — An ontological relation under which one target's obtaining would be conditional on a specified ground, without that dependence being presently operative.

ORI:220 — persistent shared-world constraint — A persistent ontological relation that limits which states may coherently obtain across one shared reality, independently of whether it is presently operative.
ORI:221 — operative shared-world constraint — An ontological relation that is presently limiting which states may coherently obtain across one shared reality.
ORI:222 — latent shared-world constraint — An ontological relation that belongs to the admissible order of one shared reality without presently limiting which states obtain within it.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode causal mechanisms, provenance history, temporal priority, unrestricted possibility or necessity, probability, observation, representation, formal entailment, physical or biological affordance, social permission, productive agency, data or software dependency, or structural implementation. Lexical latency is positive nonoperative membership; runtime [2]/num remains assertion-level uncertainty.
